\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{जरूरत} (jarūrat)}{जरूरत (jarūrat)}]{\mw{जरूरत} (jarūrat) — a need}

\label{lesson:MW-C112-jarurat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for hope, then the Marwadi for a demand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{जरूरत}}
\textbf{\mw{जरूरत}} — \emph{jarūrat} — \textquotedblleft{}a need\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{जरूरत}} (\emph{jarūrat}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{ḍarūra}, \textquotedblleft{}need, necessity\textquotedblright{}, which reached Marwadi through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{ḍ-r-r} (Lane). Marwadi says the \emph{ḍ}, which Persian pronounces \emph{z}, as \emph{j}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jarūrat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jarūrat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{jarūrat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for hope, then the Marwadi for a demand, then say \emph{jarūrat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{जरूरत} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A need\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{लालच} (lālach)}{लालच (lālach)}]{\mw{लालच} (lālach) — greed}

\label{lesson:MW-C112-lalach}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a demand, then the Marwadi for a need.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{लालच}}
\textbf{\mw{लालच}} — \emph{lālach} — \textquotedblleft{}greed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{लालच}} (\emph{lālach}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{lālitya}, \textquotedblleft{}amorousness\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry (CDIAL 11029); the match is through Hindi \emph{lālac}. It is built on \emph{lalita}, \textquotedblleft{}amorous\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मरजी} (marjī)}{मरजी (marjī)}]{\mw{मरजी} (marjī) — one's will, a choice}

\label{lesson:MW-C112-marji}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a dream, then the Marwadi for an expectation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मरजी}}
\textbf{\mw{मरजी}} — \emph{marjī} — \textquotedblleft{}one's will, a choice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{मरजी}} (\emph{marjī}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{marḍī}, \textquotedblleft{}pleasing, approved\textquotedblright{}, which reached Marwadi through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{r-ḍ-w} (Lane). Persian says it \emph{marzī}; Marwadi says the \emph{z} as \emph{j}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}
